subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw enable periodic memory sync by default as a fallback for missed watcher events, or keep interval sync opt-in and rely on current native watcher/error hardening?
rationale: The bug is valid and user-visible, but changing an unconfigured default from disabled to periodic background sync can affect existing users, provider usage, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Repair and land the fallback
options.body: Scope the interval dirty mark correctly, accept the 30-minute default as an intentional upgrade behavior, and close this issue through the linked PR after merge.

options.title: Keep interval sync opt-in
options.body: Leave the default at 0, document `intervalMinutes: 30` as the workaround, and decide whether current native watcher hardening is sufficient.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Pause the default change until maintainers can reproduce or observe a current-main watcher outage that survives the native watcher rework.

recommendation.title: Repair and land the fallback
recommendation.body: Scope the interval dirty mark correctly, accept the 30-minute default as an intentional upgrade behavior, and close this issue through the linked PR after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent merged history across memory watcher, memory index, and upgrade-sensitive memory storage work.
